# Objective

Build a synthetic ETF inventory with staggered listing dates and changing liquidity. Compare a current-survivor backfill with a point-in-time universe, then select one representative per exposure.

# Python

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
import pandas as pd

master = pd.DataFrame({
    "ticker": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "exposure": ["Japan", "Japan", "Brazil", "Brazil"],
    "list_date": pd.to_datetime(["2018-01-01", "2023-01-01", "2019-01-01", "2025-01-01"]),
    "adv_m": [25, 40, 18, 35],
    "history_days": [2000, 800, 1700, 300],
})

signal_date = pd.Timestamp("2024-12-31")
pt = master[(master.list_date <= signal_date) & (master.history_days >= 504) & (master.adv_m >= 10)]
rep = (pt.sort_values(["exposure", "adv_m", "history_days"], ascending=[True, False, False])
          .groupby("exposure", as_index=False).first())
print(rep[["exposure", "ticker"]])
```

# Audit questions

1. Which ticker incorrectly enters 2024 if today's survivor list is backfilled?
2. Which names are market-eligible but fail the history gate?
3. If a newer wrapper becomes the liquidity leader in 2027, from what signal month should the representative switch take effect?
4. Would that prospective switch justify rewriting the certified 2024 portfolio history? Why not?
